stem: A push or a pull on an object is called a __________.
solution: A force is a push or a pull acting on an object.

stem: A force can change the __________ of an object.
solution: A force can change an object's speed, direction of motion, or shape.

stem: When two forces act on an object in the same direction, the net force is their __________.
solution: Forces in the same direction add up to give a larger net force.

stem: When two forces act on an object in opposite directions, the net force is their __________.
solution: Forces in opposite directions subtract; the net force is their difference, in the direction of the larger force.

stem: A force applied by direct physical contact is called a __________ force.
solution: Contact forces, like muscular force and friction, act through direct contact.

stem: The force resulting from the action of muscles is called __________ force.
solution: Muscular force is exerted by the action of muscles, e.g., when we lift or push.

stem: The force that opposes the motion of one surface over another is called __________.
solution: Friction is a contact force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces.

stem: A force that acts without physical contact between objects is a __________ force.
solution: Non-contact forces, like gravity and magnetism, act without direct contact.

stem: The force exerted by a magnet is an example of a __________ force.
solution: Magnetic force is a non-contact force acting even at a distance.

stem: The force that pulls all objects towards the centre of the Earth is __________.
solution: Gravitational force (gravity) pulls objects towards the Earth's centre; it is a non-contact force.

stem: The force between two electrically charged objects is called __________ force.
solution: Electrostatic force acts between charged bodies and is a non-contact force.

stem: The force acting on a unit area of a surface is called __________.
solution: Pressure is the force acting perpendicularly on a unit area of a surface.

stem: Pressure is calculated using the formula __________.
solution: Pressure = force ÷ area on which it acts.

stem: For the same force, pressure is greater when the area is __________.
solution: Since pressure = force ÷ area, a smaller area produces greater pressure for the same force.

stem: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because a sharp edge __________.
options: has a smaller area and exerts more pressure
solution: The small area of a sharp edge concentrates the force, producing high pressure that cuts easily.

stem: The wide, flat foundations of buildings are made to __________.
options: reduce pressure on the ground by spreading the weight over a large area
solution: A large base area reduces the pressure on the ground, preventing the building from sinking.

stem: The pressure exerted by a liquid __________ with depth.
solution: Liquid pressure increases with depth, which is why dams are built thicker at the bottom.

stem: A dam is made thicker at the bottom than at the top because __________.
options: water pressure is greater at the bottom
water pressure is the same everywhere
solution: Since liquid pressure increases with depth, the dam must be thicker at the bottom to withstand it.

stem: Liquids exert pressure on the __________ of their container.
solution: Liquids exert pressure on both the bottom and the walls of the container.

stem: Gases also exert pressure on the walls of their container. An inflated balloon stays firm because of __________.
options: the pressure of the enclosed air
solution: The enclosed air exerts pressure on the balloon's walls, keeping it inflated.

stem: The pressure exerted by the layer of air surrounding the Earth is called __________.
solution: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the air (atmosphere) around us.

stem: We are not crushed by atmospheric pressure because __________.
options: the pressure of blood/fluids inside our body balances it
solution: The pressure of fluids inside our body balances the outside atmospheric pressure, so we are not crushed.

stem: A rubber sucker sticks to a smooth surface because of __________.
options: atmospheric pressure pushing it onto the surface
solution: Pressing out the air creates low pressure inside; higher atmospheric pressure outside holds the sucker in place.

stem: Which of the following shows that a force can change the shape of an object?
options: Pressing a lump of dough flattens it
solution: Pressing dough changes its shape, showing a force can deform an object.

stem: A camel can walk easily on sand because its broad feet __________.
options: spread its weight over a larger area, reducing pressure
solution: Broad feet spread the camel's weight over a larger area, lowering the pressure so it does not sink in sand.

stem: School bags have wide straps rather than thin strings because wide straps __________.
options: reduce the pressure on the shoulders
solution: Wide straps spread the weight over a larger area, reducing pressure and discomfort on the shoulders.

stem: The nails and pins are made pointed (with a small tip area) so that they __________.
options: exert high pressure to pierce easily
solution: A small tip area concentrates the force into high pressure, allowing the nail or pin to pierce easily.

stem: The SI unit of force is the __________.
solution: The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

stem: The SI unit of pressure is the __________.
solution: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), equal to one newton per square metre.

stem: When two teams pull a rope in a tug of war, the rope moves towards the team applying __________ force.
solution: The rope moves towards the team exerting the greater force, in the direction of the net force.

stem: If two equal and opposite forces act on a stationary object, the object __________.
solution: Equal and opposite (balanced) forces cancel out, leaving no net force, so the object stays at rest.

stem: The effect of a force depends on its __________.
solution: A force's effect depends on both its size (magnitude) and its direction.

stem: Gravitational force acting on an object is felt as its __________.
solution: The weight of an object is the gravitational force with which the Earth pulls it.

stem: A porter places a cloth pad on his head while carrying loads to __________.
options: increase the area of contact and reduce pressure
solution: The pad increases the contact area, reducing the pressure of the load on the head.

stem: Why do deep-sea divers wear special suits?
options: To withstand the high water pressure at great depths
solution: Water pressure increases with depth, so divers wear special suits to withstand the high pressure deep underwater.

stem: The pressure exerted by a gas increases when it is __________.
options: compressed into a smaller volume or heated
solution: Compressing a gas or heating it increases its pressure.

stem: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
options: Force of a bat on a ball
solution: Gravity acts at a distance (non-contact); friction and muscular force are contact forces.

stem: Air pressure decreases as we go __________.
solution: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, as the air becomes thinner higher up.

stem: A force applied on an object at rest can __________.
solution: A force on a stationary object can start it moving.

stem: The tractors and heavy vehicles have wide tyres to __________.
options: reduce pressure on the ground so they do not sink
solution: Wide tyres spread the vehicle's weight over a larger area, lowering the pressure so it does not sink into soft ground.

stem: Which of the following will exert the most pressure on the ground?
options: A woman standing on a pointed heel
The same woman standing on flat shoes
solution: A pointed heel has a very small contact area, so it exerts the highest pressure for the same weight.

stem: The direction of the force of friction is always __________ the direction of motion.
solution: Friction always acts opposite to the direction of motion, opposing it.

stem: A balloon is pressed harder on one side; it changes shape, showing a force can __________.
options: change the shape of an object
solution: Pressing the balloon deforms it, showing that a force can change an object's shape.

stem: A change in the speed of a moving object is brought about by a __________.
solution: Applying a force can speed up, slow down, or change the direction of a moving object.

stem: A liquid in a container transmits pressure __________.
solution: A liquid exerts and transmits pressure in all directions within the container.

stem: Which of the following correctly relates force, pressure and area?
options: For a fixed force, smaller area → higher pressure
For a fixed force, larger area → higher pressure
solution: Pressure = force/area, so for a fixed force a smaller area gives a higher pressure.

stem: A straw works because when we suck, we lower the pressure inside, and __________ pushes the drink up.
solution: Sucking reduces pressure inside the straw; the greater atmospheric pressure on the drink pushes it up the straw.

stem: The force of gravity gives us our __________, which can differ on the Moon.
solution: Weight depends on gravity, so an object weighs less on the Moon (weaker gravity), though its mass stays the same.

stem: The SI unit of pressure, one newton per square metre, is called the __________.
solution: One pascal (Pa) equals one newton per square metre, the SI unit of pressure.

stem: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the __________.
options: weight of the air above us
solution: Atmospheric pressure results from the weight of the column of air in the atmosphere pressing down.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Force and Pressure' is that:
options: a force is a push or pull that can change motion or shape, and pressure is force per unit area, both explaining many everyday phenomena
force and pressure are the same
pressure does not depend on area
solution: The chapter explains forces (contact and non-contact) and pressure (force per unit area), applying them to everyday situations.

stem: A force can change the __________ of a moving object.
solution: A force can change the speed and direction of a moving object.

stem: A force can also change the __________ of an object.
solution: A force can change the shape of an object, e.g. squeezing dough.

stem: Forces that act only when objects are in contact are called __________ forces.
solution: Contact forces, like muscular and friction forces, act on touching objects.

stem: Forces that act without physical contact are called __________ forces.
solution: Non-contact forces such as gravity and magnetism act at a distance.

stem: The force exerted by our muscles is a __________ force.
solution: Muscular force is a contact force exerted by muscles.

stem: The force of attraction between any two objects due to their mass is __________ force.
solution: Gravitational force is the attraction between objects due to their masses.

stem: The force between two charged objects is called __________ force.
solution: Electrostatic force acts between electric charges.

stem: When two forces act in the same direction, the net force is their __________.
solution: Forces in the same direction add up.

stem: When two forces act in opposite directions, the net force is their __________.
solution: Opposing forces subtract to give the net force.

stem: The force per unit area on a surface is called __________.
solution: Pressure is the force acting per unit area.

stem: A sharp knife cuts better than a blunt one because its thin edge exerts __________.
solution: The small edge area concentrates force into a high pressure, cutting easily.

stem: Liquid pressure __________ with depth.
solution: Liquid pressure increases with depth due to the weight of liquid above.

stem: The pressure exerted by the weight of air is called __________ pressure.
solution: Atmospheric pressure is due to the weight of the air above us.

stem: Atmospheric pressure __________ as we go higher in the atmosphere.
solution: Air is thinner at higher altitudes, so atmospheric pressure decreases.

stem: A camel walks easily on sand because its broad feet __________.
solution: Broad feet spread the weight over a larger area, reducing pressure.

stem: The straps of a heavy bag are made wide to __________.
solution: A wider strap spreads the force over a larger area, reducing pressure on the shoulder.

stem: The magnetic force between two magnets acts __________.
solution: Magnetic force is a non-contact force that acts at a distance.

stem: Which of the following pairs are both non-contact forces?
solution: Gravitational and magnetic forces both act without contact.

stem: A charged plastic straw attracts small pieces of paper due to __________ force.
solution: The charged straw attracts paper by electrostatic force.

stem: The effect of a force depends on its magnitude and its __________.
solution: A force is described by both magnitude and direction.

stem: Dam walls are made thicker at the bottom because liquid pressure is __________ there.
solution: Liquid pressure is highest at the bottom, so dams are thicker there.

stem: The nib of a pen is pointed to __________.
options: exert high pressure over a small area
solution: A small tip gives high pressure, letting the pen mark easily.

stem: Air, like liquids, exerts pressure __________.
solution: Air (a fluid) exerts pressure in all directions.

stem: An object thrown upward falls back due to __________ force.
solution: Earth's gravitational force pulls the object back down.

stem: Two equal and opposite forces acting on an object produce a net force of __________.
solution: Equal and opposite forces cancel, giving zero net force.

stem: We do not feel crushed by atmospheric pressure because __________.
options: the pressure inside our body balances it
solution: The pressure inside our body equals the atmospheric pressure, balancing it.
